text:
nightly-bench-bot: [ALERT] nightly eval (2026-03-18 03:12 UTC) — quality regression flagged for model redwood-v1 against PromptBank v9. Overall EM -4.7% vs baseline. Affected prompt groups: date-normalization, negation-heavy. CI details: https://ci.internal/runs/48291 🔍

anya: saw the bot. quick sanity check — was there a prompt bank push last night?

ben: yep, merged PB update #814 by eva at 23:45 UTC. It added a handful of negation edgecases and rewrote ~6 date-normalization examples.

anya: can you paste the small diff? no need for full PR.

ben: sure — snippet from the merged file:
```diff
- Given the date "03/04/05", what is the canonical ISO date?
+ Given the date "03/04/05", interpret year semantics and return ISO (YYYY-MM-DD).
+ Example: "03/04/05" -> "2005-03-04" (US) OR "2003-04-05" (ambig) — choose conservative parse.
```

maria: hmmm that change added ambiguity-handling text. Could change model behavior on short two-digit years. That could easily alter scoring if our eval expects deterministic canonicalization.

anya: CI details show most regressions concentrated on prompts with explicit negation and on the date group where we added the "conservative parse" instruction. sample bad gen from nightly run:

ben: ```
Prompt: "Is it false that the device never connected?"
Expected: "No, it did connect at 2026-02-11 14:02"
Model: "Yes, it never connected."  <-- direct negation flip (hallucination)
```

devin: that looks like a calibration/anchor issue introduced when we added modal/clarity text to prompts. Not necessarily model regression, more prompt semantics changed. But net result = quality drop in our eval metrics.

eva: I'm the author of the PR. I added conservative parse guidance because we were getting inconsistent ISO outputs across versions. I can revert the 2-line change or we can update the eval expectations. Which is preferred for short term?

anya: short-term: revert the prompt change to restore baseline metrics and then iterate on a targeted promptset update with controlled evals. We don't want nightly breaking product customers.

maria: agree. Requesting formal rollback approval from @devin and @eva. If both approve, I'll merge a rollback PR.

devin: approve — rollback makes sense until we craft a stable expansion of date handling. :thumbsup:

eva: approve the rollback. I'll open a follow-up PR with a smaller, test-driven prompt add (and include example-driven evals).

anya: thanks. ben can you open the rollback PR and link here? also add a short postmortem note in the PR description referencing the nightly alert id.

ben: opening #819 now. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/promptbank/pull/819 (rollback PB update #814) — will request quick review from maria/anya.

nightly-bench-bot: Noted — dropping severity to "mitigated" because rollback in progress. Re-run scheduled nightly eval will pick up new baseline once PR is merged.

maria: action items captured: 1) rollback PR 819 (ben) 2) eva to craft a smaller, test-covered prompt update + unit evals 3) update CI to flag ambiguous prompt edits automatically (proposal in PR 820).

anya: minor follow-up: can we add a small gating check that detects added phrases like "choose conservative" or extra parsing instructions in prompt diffs? those are high-risk.

ben: good call. I'll prototype a diff-lint that checks for phrase patterns and adds a reviewer tag. Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/promptbank/issues/821

devin: thanks team. keeping this thread for rollback updates.

eva: sorry about the churn — learned, will be more conservative next time. :)

ben: PR 819 merged at 2026-03-18 04:16 UTC. nightly-bench-bot: please re-evaluate when you have next run and report delta.

nightly-bench-bot: Re-eval scheduled. I will post updates in this thread when finished.
